title: Cheapest Roller J-Hooks for home gym owners
summary: NH explains why roller J-cups beat steel or plastic-lined J-cups for heavy squatting and how he got a pair for about 30 dollars instead of roughly 300. He buys brand-specific roller cups, has a welder cut off the incompatible guard, and replaces the guard with a strap looped through the rack's side holes.
claims: Steel J-cups let the bar slide but gradually wear down the knurling, reducing the bar's grip and resale value, especially when shifting heavy squats
Plastic-lined J-cups protect the bar but resist sliding; around 400 lb it becomes almost impossible to shift the bar and you can hurt yourself forcing it
Roller J-cups hold the bar but offer no resistance side to side; if you squat heavy you need them
Roller J-cups sell for around 300 dollars a pair versus 10-30 for normal ones, a markup due to lack of competition rather than material cost; prices will drop once big brands make them
Hack: buy roller J-cups made for another brand's rack (hole sizes are standard, only pillar width differs) and have the angled rear guard cut off
Do not cut metal yourself without proper tools; pay a welder about 20 dollars to cut it, and optionally paint the cut black
Replace the removed guard with a strong strap looped through the rack's side pin holes and tightened, so the cup cannot tip forward under a loaded bar
He has squatted with this setup for about five months without the cups ever moving
Side holes are spaced farther apart than front holes, so you may have to set the cups a bit lower, slightly worsening your unrack position
His roller cups cost about 30 dollars, less than his Rogue J-cups; the hack should cost about 50 instead of 300-350
Roller cups also make rolling the bar forward and backward much easier than regular J-cups
